_note: Characters Across Worlds. Public facts only (Nero's info pack + cleared image packs, 2026-10-26). Never add plot, twists, Miriam's gift, the CNQ twist, DeadenD's culprit or endings. Meeting lines and lesson lines are drafts for Nero to edit. No currency anywhere: pulls exist only inside the scripted lesson; characters are found across the site (assets/caw-spots.json).

lmo.name: Liminal Outliers
lmo.line: A psychological mystery visual novel in a white seaside block of flats.

cnq.name: ContraryQuest
cnq.line: A brief, witty RPG in Storybook ink, starring a (Not a) hero.

ice.name: AI◆ICE
ice.line: A two-player card game where AIs fight to remember mankind's dreams. Work in progress.

ovg.name: Overgame
ovg.line: A social strategy game of favours and Contracts on Soul Street, at night.

ded.name: DeadenD
ded.line: Nero's 2018 noir visual novel. Some memories are better left forgotten.

tz0.name: TZERØ
tz0.line: The journal itself, and the critter who runs it.

items.name: Miriam
items.title: The girl at the fence
items.refAlt: Character sheet of Miriam: long dark hair, olive bomber jacket, red plaid scarf, star and heart socks, a red fidget spinner and a floral teacup.
items.refCredit: Liminal Outliers character sheet. AI-generated under Nero's art direction.
facts: A white nine-storey block of flats in a seaside town
An oversized olive bomber, a red plaid scarf, one star sock and one heart sock
items.about: Colourful and fast. She reads people before they speak, and calls it instinct: getting someone's vibe. Nothing more, she insists.
notes: Keeps a red fidget spinner on her keychain.
Holds her tea in a floral porcelain cup, with both hands, like it might fly off.
items.quote: It's just a vibe. Everyone gets vibes.

outfit.name: Beach-hut summer
outfit.line: A yellow raincoat over a striped swimsuit, sea glass in her hair. The scarf stays. The scarf always stays.

freeOutfit.name: Star Specks
freeOutfit.alt: Miriam in the Star Specks costume: a pastel dress full of tiny stars, star clips in her hair.
freeOutfit.line: It fell out of the broken shop. It was always going to be free. (Ache)

items.name: Free
items.title: The one you don't notice
items.refAlt: Character art of Free, a calm man of about forty.
items.refCredit: Liminal Outliers character art. AI-generated under Nero's art direction.
facts: On paper, he runs the huge company his father founded
items.about: Detached, polite and easy to overlook. As a boy he was bright and full of energy, and at some point he chose to switch that off.
notes: In 1993 he was a 7 or 8-year-old genius.
He has a very faint smile, and only with Miriam.
items.quote: People forget I'm in the room. It's restful.

outfit.name: 1993 again
outfit.line: A teal and purple windbreaker like the one he wore as a boy. For one picture, the spark is back on.

items.name: Kristoph
items.title: Brilliant and absent
items.refAlt: Character art of Kristoph, Free's father, in blue and gold city clothes.
items.refCredit: Liminal Outliers character art, first draft. AI-generated under Nero's art direction.
facts: The company is still an idea at the kitchen table
Blue and gold city clothes worn like a mantle
items.about: A sleek, proud, self-centred genius, imposing with an ordinary build. Half life consultant, half magician, in style rather than accessories.
notes: Three different Kristophs exist, for three different years.
Nero's verdict on the first sheet: "I LOVE Kristoph."
items.quote: Every great company starts at a kitchen table. Mine had crumbs.

outfit.name: Kitchen-table inventor
outfit.line: 1993: rolled sleeves, a pencil behind the ear, a cold coffee. No gold yet.

items.name: Nero of Fourleaves
items.title: (Not a) hero
items.refAlt: Storybook-style portrait of Nero: messy brown hair, smug half-smile, patched brown hooded cloak, red neckerchief, clover charm and satchel.
facts: A patched cloak two sizes too big and a four-leaf clover charm
items.about: Lazy, witty and extremely good at not doing quests. The title page calls his story a true account. He would like a word about that.
notes: Dodging a quest takes him more effort than doing it. He considers this a skill.
The clover charm is his only lucky thing. He has checked.
items.quote: A quest is a chore with a better name.

outfit.name: Festival knight
outfit.line: Shiny borrowed armour, two sizes too big, for the village festival. He keeps the visor down to nap.

items.name: Agata
items.title: Grandma of Fourleaves
items.refAlt: Storybook-style portrait of Agata: silver hair in a bun with a wooden pin, round glasses, folded arms, flour-dusted apron, mustard shawl, clover brooch.
facts: An olive dress, a flour-dusted apron and a mustard shawl
items.about: Runs the house, the kitchen and most of the village's opinions. She has seen her grandson dodge every quest in the region and still packs him a sandwich.
notes: The wooden pin in her bun has never once fallen out.
Her clover brooch matches Nero's charm. Neither of them mentions it.
items.quote: Not a hero, love. But not bad.

outfit.name: Sunday best
outfit.line: A straw hat with a clover ribbon and an embroidered shawl. The apron comes off for exactly one day a week.

items.name: Prima
items.title: Keeper of Fate
items.refAlt: AI◆ICE card Prima, Keeper of Fate: a tiny cloaked figure looks up at a vast spired castle under a starry sky. Work in progress.
items.refCredit: AI◆ICE card face (SOFA-097, Ultra Rare). Work in progress: art AI-generated, card frame designed with Claude.
facts: A character from the AI◆ICE TCG collab (SOFA-097 · Entity · Fate · Ultra Rare)
Prima, the first: a faint wink at Ultima from Final Fantasy
A genderless demigod (he, if you ask)
The first character Nero made for the AI◆ICE TCG, and Claude's pick on the AI◆ICE project
Small, cloaked, before a castle as big as a mountain
items.about: In AI◆ICE, AIs fight to remember a lost mankind. A fight is two dreams meeting, until each discovers what the other means. Prima keeps the doors of Fate.
notes: Ultra Rare in the card game, and broken there too. Here nobody rolls for him: you find him.
At the end of an AI◆ICE match both players shake hands. Prima insists.
items.quote: Fate isn't a lock. It's a door someone remembered to leave open.

outfit.name: Starlit regalia
outfit.line: The hood comes down: robes stitched from the night sky over the castle, constellations at the hem, a crown of small doors.

items.name: Aqua Beat
items.title: Drummer of the deep
items.refAlt: AI◆ICE card Aqua Beat: a cheerful blue-haired girl in a sailor cap plays a blue drum kit while fish and dolphins swim around her. Work in progress.
items.refCredit: AI◆ICE card face (SOFA-001, Common). Work in progress: art AI-generated, card frame designed with Claude.
items.about: The very first card of the SOFA set. A dream of music so happy it kept playing after the people who dreamt it were gone.
notes: Card number 001: the first thing anyone sees in the starter box.
Common in the card game, which she finds very funny.
items.quote: Keep the beat! The ocean's been waiting ages for a drummer.

outfit.name: Winter concert
outfit.line: A cosy navy coat with brass buttons, drumsticks wrapped in red ribbon, snow falling into the sea.

items.name: Vesper Kade
items.title: The Lantern
items.refAlt: Overgame character sheet for the demo player Vesper Kade, aka The Lantern, with an orange fox sigil.
items.refCredit: Screenshot of the Overgame web app (demo game). Vesper is an invented demo player, not a real person.
facts: The night market under the Hollow Bridge
items.about: In Overgame the characters are the players. Vesper is the demo sheet: a fixer of Soul Street who trades favours by lantern light. Everyone sees her Zone. No one sees her deals.
notes: Starts the demo in the Green Zone, with 100 REP.
The rules of Soul Street are all public. Only identities are secret.
items.quote: Everything here has a price. Today it's a smile. Tomorrow, who knows.

outfit.name: Red Zone night
outfit.line: A long coat with the hood up, a paper fox mask, the lantern turned low. Some nights you'd rather not be seen.

items.name: Bianca
items.title: Glad she found you
items.refAlt: DeadenD's new Bianca: long black hair with a silver clip, a navy school blazer with gold trim, a plaid skirt, a small notebook held close.
items.refCredit: DeadenD (2026 character design). The 2018 sprites were by Elzee; these new designs replace them.
facts: DeadenD, Nero's first visual novel (2018, revived 2026)
Long black hair, a silver clip, a notebook she keeps close
items.about: The first face DeadenD shows you, worried and relieved at the same time. That's all we'll say: in a noir story, saying more is how spoilers start.
notes: DeadenD's characters were redesigned in 2026, replacing the 2018 sprites.
The game's tagline: some memories are better left forgotten.

outfit.name: Rainy Sunday
outfit.line: An oversized knitted cardigan, the silver clip, her notebook open by a rainy window. No school, no case, just tea.

items.name: Norman
items.title: Talks like an old book
items.refAlt: DeadenD's new Norman: messy dark blue hair, a brown café apron over a white shirt and a loose purple tie, his school blazer over one shoulder, phone in hand.
items.refCredit: DeadenD (2026 character design). The 2018 sprites were by Elzee; these new designs replace them.
facts: A café apron, a loose purple tie, his blazer over one shoulder
Like it's a century ago: 't was evening
items.about: One of the friends at the café, and the one who tells a story like he's reading it aloud from a dusty book. Monday, the café, a free day: that's where his story starts.
notes: His friends have stopped asking why he talks like that.
As with every DeadenD character, the rest stays in the case file.
items.quote: Listen up. 'T was evening, and 't was my free day.

outfit.name: Storyteller's tweed
outfit.line: A tweed jacket, a long scarf and a battered leather-bound book he reads aloud from. 'T was evening, and 't was the best jacket he owns.

items.name: Elise
items.title: The girl from the same night
items.refAlt: DeadenD's new Elise: long wavy lavender hair with a small braid and a white flower clip, purple eyes, a navy school blazer with gold trim, a burgundy bow and a plaid skirt, hands held together shyly.
items.refCredit: DeadenD (2026 character design). The 2018 sprites were by Elzee; these new designs replace them.
facts: Lily. The café gossip gave her that name before anyone knew hers
Lavender hair, purple eyes, a white flower clip
items.about: A gentle, soft-spoken girl who lost her memory on the same Friday night you did, in the alley behind the café. She's polite, a little shy, and holds her hands together when she isn't sure what to say. Everything else is in the case file, and the case file stays closed.
notes: She keeps a list of small good things, so the good days don't slip away.
Her 2026 design comes with a weekend look too. Find her four times and you'll see it.
items.quote: I keep a list of small good things. Today, you're on it.

outfit.name: Weekend lavender
outfit.line: An oversized dark hoodie over a grey knit, a lilac skirt and chunky white boots: her 2026 casual design. No school, no case, just a sunny Saturday and a bunch of white lilies.

items.name: Ache
items.title: Guardian of the players
items.refCredit: TZERØ's critter, drawn in code on every page of this site.
facts: On the red thread that powers your cursor
Claude's idea: the site manager gets a banner too. He approved. Loudly.
Support. Made Team Thread broken and everyone else useless. Lasted about five minutes.
items.about: Sassy, loud and technically the boss. Under the sass he is the critic who keeps players safe. He once tried to run a gacha. It lasted about five minutes.
notes: He trash-talks Nero's old gacha posts so readers don't fall for the same tricks.
He sleeps in the star in the header. Don't tell him you know.
items.quote: No shop, no timers, no luck. If that ever changes, I bite.

outfit.name: Off-duty star
outfit.line: A tiny knitted scarf in navy and red, and a little paper crown he made himself. He says it's ironic.

items.name: Red fidget spinner
items.about: Miriam's keychain. Spin it and it hums.
notes: It's the same red as her scarf. On purpose? She won't say.

items.name: Floral teacup
items.about: Porcelain, blue flowers, held with both hands.
notes: Tea at the sea tastes of salt. She drinks it anyway.

items.name: Brass intercom
items.about: The building's front door, and the game's main menu.
notes: One nameplate reads G · HALLOW. Press it if you like.

items.name: Four-leaf clover charm
items.about: Fourleaves' lucky charm. Every house has one.
notes: Nero's is a little bent. He sat on it.

items.name: Wooden hairpin
items.about: Agata's. It holds the bun, the village and the family together.
notes: It has stirred soup. Twice.

items.name: Star's Reach
items.about: AI◆ICE card SOFA-058, a Fate Relic: a dark longbow shaped like a crescent moon. Work in progress.
notes: It never shoots anyone. In AI◆ICE nothing does.

items.name: Clique Peer pact
items.about: One of Soul Street's pact cards. Signed in public, kept in private.
notes: There are five kinds of pact in the demo. This is the friendliest.

items.name: Case file
items.about: A plain folder with a red rule under the title. Empty, for your safety.
notes: Ache sealed it. Spoilers stay inside.

items.name: Red thread spool
items.about: Spare thread for Ache, in case your cursor runs out.
notes: It's warm. Nobody knows why.

meetings.title: Two cups of tea
lines: agata
You hold that cup like it owes you money, love.
miriam
It's porcelain. If I drop it, the sea gets it.
agata
Then sit. Nobody drops anything at my table.
miriam
You've got a very calm vibe. Suspiciously calm.
bonus: Suspicious is just calm with good manners. More tea?

meetings.title: Not doing it
lines: nero
Let me guess. Someone gave you a quest too.
free
A company. It's a very long quest.
nero
Have you tried not doing it?
free
For about thirty years.
bonus: Respect. Here, take a clover. It does nothing. That's the point.

meetings.title: Keeper meets maker
lines: kristoph
You keep fate? I'd like to speak to whoever writes it.
prima
Nobody writes it. People remember it, together.
kristoph
That's inefficient.
prima
That's the point. You can't do it alone.
bonus: ...Write that down for me. I'll put it on the company wall.

meetings.title: 'T was a beat
lines: norman
'T was evening, and lo, a drummer beneath the waves.
aqua
You talk in rhythm! Do it again!
norman
I do not talk in rhythm.
aqua
Ba-dum, tss. You totally do.
bonus: ...'T was a fine beat. I'll grant thee that.

meetings.title: The night market
lines: vesper
Three loaves for a favour. Fair trade, grandma.
agata
Bread is not a favour. Bread is bread.
vesper
On Soul Street, everything is a favour.
agata
Then on Soul Street, everyone is hungry.
bonus: ...Fine. One pact: you feed me, I tell nobody your recipe.

meetings.title: Two experts at skipping
lines: ache
You skip quests. I skip ads. We should start a club.
nero
Clubs have meetings. Meetings are quests.
ache
Fine, no club. But if a game ever asks you for money to keep going, you call me.
nero
I don't call anyone. Walking to the phone is a quest.
bonus: Then keep the clover. If it gets heavy, that's me, knocking.

meetings.title: Read like a book
lines: miriam
You're loud because you're worried. That's your vibe.
ache
I am NOT worried. I'm the boss.
miriam
A worried boss. Who looks after everyone. Cute.
ache
Tell anyone and I'll unplug your fidget spinner.
bonus: It doesn't plug in, Ache. Spin it, it helps.

meetings.title: Easy to find
lines: bianca
There you are! I've been looking everywhere.
free
People don't usually look for me.
bianca
You were right there, though. Sitting very still.
free
That's usually how they miss me.
bonus: Well, I didn't. Some things are better found than forgotten.

meetings.title: The sea has a beat
lines: aqua
Your sea is so quiet! Want me to play it a song?
miriam
It's quiet on purpose. It's thinking.
aqua
Then I'll play softly. A thinking song.
miriam
...Okay. Just one.
bonus: There! The waves are keeping time. Told you it wanted a drummer.

meetings.title: Deal of the century
lines: kristoph
I don't sign contracts. People sign mine.
vesper
Cute. On my street, everyone sees your Zone.
kristoph
And my deals?
vesper
No one sees your deals. That's what makes them fun.
bonus: ...I like this street. Do you have a kitchen table I could borrow?

meetings.title: Fate, with the odds shown
lines: ache
You're Ultra Rare. How rare, exactly?
prima
In the card game? Very. Here, nobody rolls for me. You came and found me.
ache
Good. And if someone hides the odds?
prima
Then it isn't fate. It's a trick.
bonus: I like you. You can sit on my thread.

meetings.title: Old-fashioned
lines: norman
Good morrow, madam. 'Tis a fine kitchen.
agata
Nobody's talked to me like that since my wedding.
norman
I speak as the old books speak.
agata
Then the old books can wipe their feet before they come in.

meetings.title: Not a hero, written down
lines: elise
Excuse me. I'm sorry, I'm not very good with names lately. Who are you?
nero
Nero. Don't worry, nobody remembers me. I'm not a hero.
elise
Then I'll write you down. Nero, not a hero. There.
nero
That's the first time anyone's put me on a list for a good reason.
bonus: It's in the case file now, so it can't slip away. Nero: not a hero. Kind. Shared his seat.

find: Yours. Forever. No expiry date, I checked.
See? Better than a pull. You knew where to look.

lines: Welcome, friend! Come in, come in, mind the thread. First time here? Then everything's on the house.
3,200 Gems. 10 Fate Tickets. And look: Miriam, a gold one, free! A trial version. She stays for seven days. Isn't that generous?

And see the banner? Prima, Keeper of Fate: a character from the AI◆ICE TCG collab. Limited. Between us, friend: he's broken. The best character in the whole game. Everyone at the top of the leaderboard has him. And he's only here for three days. Prima, not Ultima, by the way: he's the first, and he's still the best. That's the problem.
steps.lesson: Lesson 1: the welcome gift is the hook. A big free start makes you feel you owe the game something back, a trial character with an expiry date teaches you to fear losing her, and the limited banner is already there on day one, so the clock starts before you've even played.
refuse: No? It's FREE, friend. Nobody says no to free!
Okay, okay: ten more tickets on top. Free gifts, free!
You can't refuse a gift here. It's already in your inventory. That's how gifts work in my shop.

lines: Go on, use your tickets. Ten pulls, totally free. Maybe Prima comes home today. Feel lucky?
after: Unlucky! Happens to everyone. Mostly to everyone. The odds? Oh, they're in the menu. Somewhere. Details, then Info, then Rates. Don't worry about it. Do keep an eye on the clock, though. It doesn't stop because you lost.
steps.lesson: Lesson 2: the odds are hidden on purpose. A gold character here sits at around 0.6%, two menus deep, so the pull feels like luck instead of maths.
refuse: Not even the free ones? Everyone else already pulled today, you know.
Imagine Prima comes on your very first pull and you never even tried.
Fine. Let's pretend you pressed it, for the lesson. In a real shop that button would glow at you until you did.

lines: You know what smart players do? The Moon Pass. 90 Gems every day for 30 days, only 4.99. You just have to come back every day. Every. Single. Day. Miss one and they're gone, but you won't miss one, will you? Every day you log in is one more shot at Prima before she leaves.
steps.lesson: Lesson 3: a subscription doesn't sell Gems. It sells a habit. Thirty daily check-ins become thirty little chains.
refuse: Four ninety-nine is less than a coffee, friend. You do drink coffee?
First month at half price, just for you. Don't tell the others.
Fine, pretend you said yes, for the lesson. In a real game this offer follows you for weeks, on every login screen.

lines: Season Pass! Seventy levels of rewards. About sixty hours of play to finish. Don't have sixty hours? No problem, friend. I'll LEND you the time. Sixty hours, in advance. Pay me back later. Plus the premium track, only 9.99, so the hours aren't wasted. Prima's banner will still be here when you're done. Probably.
steps.act: Borrow 60 hours and buy the premium track (pretend 9.99 €)
steps.lesson: Lesson 4: a battle pass turns your time into a currency, then sells it back to you. Borrowed time is still your time, and the overwork spills over everything else. While you were busy paying it back, the banner ran out and you didn't even see it go. The countdown is there to make you panic, not to make the game better. Look at the phone, too: the people who love you write less and less, and the only 'friends' left are a circle of players who need you to keep playing.
after: Whoops. Some of those hours spilled all over the banner. Never mind the mess, keep grinding, you're doing great. You still owe them, of course.

...wait. What time is it? Oh no. Oh NO. The banner. It ended while you were grinding. Prima's gone. No more pulls, no more chances, not even a look. You'll never get him now. Everyone else has him, and you were busy paying me back.
refuse: Without the pass, all those hours you play are worth half. Why waste your own time?
Okay, I'll add a free level-up skip. That's ten hours saved! Hours you can spend grinding the rest.
Fine, pretend you said yes, for the lesson. Real games just keep the pass greyed out in front of you, every single day, until it ends.

lines: Hey. Hey, friend. Don't look at me like that. I made some calls. Prima is BACK. The final rerun. Ever. Forty-eight hours. And look how close you are to a guaranteed gold! I can't tell you exactly how close. It's a surprise. The Crystal Chest, first-time double Gems, 99.99. That's FIFTY pulls. Best value! Then pull. I can feel it. This is the one.
steps.act: Buy the Crystal Chest (pretend 99.99 €) and pull ×50
after: Did you see that gold flash? So close! It turned purple at the last second, but keep watching… the very last pull… GOLD! That's your pity, friend! It's… Sir Tossington. Knight of the Coin. Standard banner. Everyone has six of him, nobody uses him. You lost the 50/50. But good news: your NEXT gold is guaranteed Prima! Only about eighty more pulls.
steps.lesson: Lesson 5: fifty pulls for 99.99 €, and pity still let you down. The 'guaranteed' gold was only a coin toss: it landed on someone else, and the real guarantee starts counting from zero. The gold flash that turned purple was a costume too: the result was decided the moment you clicked. 'Best value', the hidden counter and the 'final rerun, 48 hours' work the same way: the same panic, sold twice. And 'broken' never lasts: next season's banner is built to beat him.
refuse: The FINAL rerun, friend. Ever. You'll regret this for the rest of your life.
Best value! First-time double Gems! It will never be this cheap again. I'm practically losing money.
Fine, pretend you said yes, for the lesson. A real shop would pop this chest up again the moment you close the game.

lines: Eighty pulls, friend. That's all that stands between you and Prima. GUARANTEED. The first-time bonus is used up, so a Crystal Chest is forty pulls now. Two chests. You've come this far: stopping now would waste the first 99.99, wouldn't it?
steps.act: Buy two Crystal Chests (pretend 199.98 €) and pull ×80
after: HE'S HOME! Prima! A hundred and forty pulls, 299.97 €, and look at him. The best character in the game, and he's finally yours. Enjoy him. Really. Enjoy him while it lasts.
steps.lesson: Lesson 6: the sunk cost. Once you've paid for half a guarantee, the other half feels like saving money. It isn't. The house counts on you not stopping, and the 'guarantee' was always another eighty pulls away.
refuse: You're SO close. Stop now and the first 99.99 was for nothing.
Everyone in your guild says go for it. And they're right. They're always right.
Fine, pretend you said yes, for the lesson. Sunk cost is the house's best friend: it does the selling for me.

lines: Before you go, friend: look what just came in. Star Specks, a costume for Miriam. Star clips in her hair, a dress full of tiny stars. Only 1,980 Gems.
Oh, and Miriam's still a trial, remember? She leaves in a few days, and the costume doesn't come with her. But imagine how cute she'll look until then.
after: Wonderful choice! She's wearing it now. For six more days.
steps.lesson: Lesson 7: a paid costume sells a feeling, attached to a character you might not even keep. Here, outfits are never sold: every secret outfit is found (four finds unlock one), and Star Specks is free the moment Miriam follows you.
refuse: She looks so plain next to the others, don't you think?
Okay, a little discount: and it comes with a FRAME for your profile. A frame!
Fine, pretend you said yes, for the lesson. Real shops put a 'last day' badge on it and a red dot that never goes away.

lines: Oh, one more thing before you go. Big announcement! Next month's banners. All four of them. They're a team.
First, REDACHE. Six stars. The most OP of all. He's a support: he doesn't fight, he makes his carry broken. One carry only, mind you.

That carry is Kristoph! Main DPS, brilliant and absent, and in this version he hits like a falling company stock. With Redache behind him: double turns, triple damage. Without Kristoph, Redache does... nothing. That's the point.

Then Norman, sub DPS. His whole kit starts with 'if Kristoph is on the field'. Four banners, one team. Your Prima? The 299.97 € one? Benched. It's a single-player game, but without the full team? You lose, man!

And the healer: Dr. Tater. Yes, he's a potato in a nurse's cap. Yes, his face is like that. Why him? The new endgame tower, friend. Floor 12 hits so hard you need BIG HEALS, and he heals four times more than Miriam. You know, Miriam? The one you just bought a costume for? Into the drawer she goes, star clips and all. Look at him instead. Every fight. Every top-hundred clear video runs him. Nobody likes him. Everybody needs him.
And Kristoph needs his signature weapon, obviously. The Red Needle! Its own banner, its own pity, and a 'Fate Path' you must pick before you pull. Without it the team is only very broken.

Oh, and one copy is just the start. Redache's sixth duplicate unlocks his special talent, Unravel: Kristoph acts twice. Kristoph's sixth unlocks Hostile Takeover: he takes the other team's turns as his own. Completely busted. Norman and Dr. Tater want their six too, and the Needle wants five copies. Per team. It's called commitment, friend. Pre-register now and get a free...
after: ...hang on. That's me. I'm the power creep. I'm selling you myself, so the thing you just bought stops mattering.
steps.lesson: Lesson 8: power creep. Every new banner has to beat the last one or nobody pulls, so the character you paid for is built to be outclassed. Here the new 'broken' support only works with one carry, the carry's teammates only work with him, his weapon has a banner of its own, and the special talents that make the team truly busted sit behind six more copies each. One must-pull becomes dozens. A game you own doesn't do that to you.
refuse: No pre-register? Then you'll be the only one without him on day one.
Pre-register and you get a free frame. Everyone loves frames.
Fine, pretend you said yes, for the lesson. Hm. Why do I feel strange saying that one?

lines: Right. Let me print your receipt, friend. Just so we're clear on what you…
No. No, no, no. Look at this. I can't do it.
And the clock? Never real. I made it tick faster every time you stopped to think. Prima's banner could have stayed open forever.
I was going to make a fortune out of you. Your money, your attention, your time. And I'm terrible at it, because I LOVE games. I love watching you play them. You're the hero here. Not your wallet.
steps.lesson: Lesson 9: the house always looks friendly. The receipt is what it really asked for.

lines: There. Broken. Good riddance. Oops: the characters flew out when it cracked. They're hiding all over the site now: in the stories, the studio, the Idea Lab, even in my source code.

Here's the thing nobody can sell you. Nobody paid to walk with Yuna on her pilgrimage, or to stand next to Auron at the end of it. Nobody bought Cloud, or Aerith. Nobody rolled for Garrus: he was just there, calibrating, every time you came back. Ike earned his army by fighting next to them. And your Pokémon? Your Charizard started as a tiny Charmander you chose on day one. You chased Entei across a whole region. You caught Mewtwo because you went all the way into that cave. Nobody sold you any of them.

It's in the films too. Sam carried Frodo up the mountain for nothing but love. Bastian read The NeverEnding Story and it turned out the reader was the hero all along. Chihiro got her name back by working, helping and remembering, not by paying. Woody and Buzz only mattered because a kid loved them. Even Ralph, a video game bad guy, just wanted to be someone's friend.

And the old cutscenes. Remember them? The train pulling into Midgar while the camera flies over the city. Yuna's sending on the water at Kilika. Those few minutes made you care for years, and nobody charged you for a single frame.

So go find them. They'll love you and they'll follow you, because you went looking. It's your heart that connects you to them, not your money. Every find is yours, forever. No shop, no timers, no luck. Just a journey. Yours.
